transcript:
This is NPR News Now, the latest headlines every hour.
>> Live from NPR News, I'm Giles Snyder.
Defense Secretary Pete Hegseth is dismissing Kentucky Republican Congressman Thomas Massey's
effort to impeach him as a stunt.
>> It's a political spectacle, a personal manifesto driven by ego and resentment.
Time for one man's final days in Congress to try to do damage to this president, this
country, and most irresponsibly, the warriors who defend it.
It's a farce and it's a stunt.
And everybody knows it.
>> Hegseth speaking Tuesday morning at his first press conference at the Pentagon in
six months.
Congressman Massey's impeachment resolution failed Tuesday.
House Republicans effectively blocked Massey's impeachment charges from being considered
on a 211 to 204 vote.
House Democratic leader Hakeem Jeffries says Democrats will have a conversation about impeaching
Hegseth when they take control of Congress.
Republicans have chosen their leaders for the new Congress that will convene in January.
Senate Republicans Tuesday opted to keep John Thune of South Dakota as their leader on the
House side, Republicans chose Judiciary Committee Chairman and Trump ally Jim Jordan of Ohio.
Lawmakers elected in Israel last month were sworn in Tuesday, opponents of Prime Minister
Benjamin Netanyahu now hold the majority in Israel's parliament, NPR's Lauren Freya reports.
>> A military band played as Israeli lawmakers filed in and took their oaths of office.
Most have pledged to support Prime Minister Netanyahu's rival Gadi Eisenkot.
Israel's President Isaac Herzog encouraged rival parties to extend a hand of compromise
and build a governing coalition.
Eisenkot is under pressure to break a campaign promise and partner with Arab-led parties,
whom Netanyahu lashed out at again, accusing them without evidence of fraud and of endangering
Israel.
Some Arab lawmakers walked out when Israel's national anthem played.
Others have submitted bills to impose term limits and repeal Netanyahu's judicial reforms.
Lauren Freya, NPR News, Tel Aviv.
>> NVIDIA shares dropped sharply for a second day after the company launched an investigation
of its CEO, who had an extramarital affair with a woman who might have been recruited
to spy for China, NPR's John Ruich reports.
>> NVIDIA share price dropped about 5.5% after falling more than 4% on Monday.
>> The route comes after a weekend announcement by the company that the board is investigating
CEO Jensen Huang.
Huang co-founded NVIDIA more than three decades ago and transformed it into one of the world's
most valuable companies.
NVIDIA makes chips that have been at the center of the AI revolution, and investors are now
pondering what the investigation might yield and what it could mean for Jensen Huang's
future at the company.
John Ruich, NPR News.
>> And you're listening to NPR News.
Researchers are expected to meet again Wednesday for a second day of talks on ending the war
in Ukraine.
The talks between Kiev and Moscow are the first since February.
They're being held in Abu Dhabi and are being mediated by the US.
The nation's largest physician group backing a near-complete ban on a popular countertop
material that's linked to an aggressive lung disease that's disabling and killing stoneworkers.
From Member Station KQED, Farida Jopla Romero reports.
The American Medical Association's new policy opposes the manufacture, sale, fabrication
and installation of high silica engineered stone for countertops and other surfaces.
Dr. Renee Bravo is a former president of the California Medical Association who pushed
for the AMA resolution.
>> This will really be a definitive rallying cry for other states to take note and develop
policies that will protect their engineered stone workers also.
Reports of stone workers have contracted silicosis in California and other states after inhaling
toxic dust while cutting engineered stone.
California regulators are set to vote next month on a rule that would phase out use of
the material.
For NPR News, I'm Farida Jopla Romero in Oakland, California.
>> The financial markets in Asia largely advancing in Wednesday trading shares in Taiwan leading
the way up more than 3% after a sharp sell-off last week in tech stocks.
Asia markets up after Wall Street lost ground following the government's latest read on
inflation.
The Labor Department said inflation ran hotter than expected last month.
This is MPC.

House Republicans block Massey's impeachment resolution on a 211-204 vote

Republicans re-elect John Thune as Senate leader and choose Jim Jordan for House leadership
Israeli lawmakers sworn in, with Netanyahu opponents now holding the parliamentary majority
NVIDIA shares fall for a second day after board launches investigation of CEO Jensen Huang
US-mediated talks on ending the Ukraine war resume in Abu Dhabi, the first since February
